title: Rust crate published to crates.io
appliesWhen: A Rust library (or binary) crate published to crates.io for others to depend on or install.
ask: Will this crate be published to crates.io? What is the minimum supported Rust version (MSRV), and is it a single crate or a workspace?

sources.title: The Cargo Book: Publishing on crates.io
The Cargo Book: The Manifest Format
The Cargo Book: Continuous Integration (verifying rust-version)

guidance: crates.io requires description and license (SPDX 2.3 expression) or license-file; also fill repository, readme, and up to 5 keywords and 5 categories (exact slugs from crates.io/category_slugs). documentation defaults to the docs.rs page.
cargo publish --dry-run only warns ("manifest has no description, license, ...") when metadata is missing; the gate treats that warning as a failure.
Publishing is permanent: a version can never be overwritten or deleted. cargo yank only stops new lockfiles from selecting it; a leaked secret must be rotated, not yanked.
Control the .crate contents with include or exclude (cargo package --list shows them); the limit is 10 MB.
Set rust-version (MSRV) and verify it in CI (cargo hack check --rust-version); changing rust-version is treated as a minor incompatibility, so document the MSRV policy (for example N-2).
Run cargo semver-checks before each release; it compares against the latest version on crates.io, so it has nothing to compare before the first release.

Trusted publishing (GitHub Actions; check crates.io docs for other providers) needs the first release published manually; then the workflow uses rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1 with id-token: write and passes the token as CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN.
Features must be additive; removing a Cargo feature or a public item is a major change, while adding a dependency is minor unless it adds new requirements such as nightly (Cargo SemVer reference).
cargo publish --dry-run leaves target/package/<crate>/Cargo.toml behind, which makes cargo semver-checks fail with "package is ambiguous"; both gate commands remove target/package.
Workspaces: cargo publish --workspace --dry-run checks all publishable members together; mark internal crates publish = false.

gates.title: cargo publish --dry-run succeeds with complete metadata
gates.command: out=$(cargo publish --dry-run --allow-dirty 2>&1); s=$?; rm -rf target/package; printf '%s\n' "$out"; [ $s -eq 0 ] && ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q 'manifest has no'
gates.architecture: Record the crate name, licence (SPDX), repository, readme, keywords/categories, and what the package includes (include/exclude); for a workspace, which members are published.
acceptance: cargo publish --dry-run packages and verifies the crate
Cargo reports no "manifest has no description, license, ..." warning

gates.title: Clippy reports no warnings
gates.architecture: Record the lint configuration ([lints] in Cargo.toml) and any allowed lints with reasons.

gates.title: Tests and doctests pass
gates.architecture: Record the test layout (unit, integration, doctests) and the feature combinations tested.

gates.title: Public API is documented and docs build without warnings
gates.architecture: Record the documentation policy (#![warn(missing_docs)], crate-level docs with an example, docs.rs features/metadata).
acceptance: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features builds with RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"
Every public item has a doc comment

gates.title: The declared rust-version (MSRV) builds
gates.setup: cargo install cargo-hack --locked (or taiki-e/install-action@cargo-hack in CI, as in the Cargo CI guide); cargo hack adds the rust-version toolchain with rustup when it is missing. Very old MSRVs may have no toolchain for newer hosts (for example Apple silicon), so run this gate in Linux CI.
gates.architecture: Record the rust-version and the MSRV policy (for example latest stable minus two releases).
acceptance: cargo hack check --rust-version passes for every publishable package

gates.title: No accidental SemVer breakage against the last published version
gates.setup: cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked (or obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks-action@v2 in CI); skip until the first release is on crates.io
gates.architecture: Record the public API surface and the versioning policy (0.x minor bumps for breaking changes, 1.x majors); breaking changes go in a changelog.
acceptance: cargo semver-checks reports no breaking changes for a minor or patch release
Each release has a changelog entry

gates.title: Releases are published from CI with trusted publishing and controlled owners
gates.architecture: Record the release workflow (tag trigger, environment, id-token: write, rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action), the owners and teams on crates.io, and how a bad release is handled (yank, new version, secret rotation).
acceptance: After the first manual release, versions are published from the CI workflow registered as a trusted publisher; no long-lived crates.io token is stored in CI
crates.io owners are listed and limited to current maintainers

gates.title: Crate licence and dependency licence compatibility need review
gates.architecture: Record the chosen licence expression and the dependencies (including build dependencies and any bundled C code) with their licences.
